findings.claim: stream_close() now waits for every entry already in _outgoing_queue to be written (_outgoing_queue_ready) before it closes write_buf, and it calls stop() only after that. mechanisms: stream_close chains write_buf.close() and stop() behind the outgoing queue drain
findings.consequence: sink.close() or the source's eof path can now take as long as the slowest queued untimed frame to send (e.g. a peer that stops reading), and shutdown_input/stop() is delayed until then. Someone diagnosing a slow or hung stream close has no documentation of this dependency. Before the patch, write_buf.close() did not wait for frames still sitting in the queue.

evidence.detail: auto queue_drained = std::exchange(_outgoing_queue_ready, make_ready_future<>());
